title: Charlemagne and the tyrants of the air

tellings.quote: It was so prominent that hysteria broke out about it in the French court and Charlemagne was considering declaring war on the tyrants of the air.

plain: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, drawing on a book called The Gods of Eden by a writer named William Bramley, tells of strange things in the skies over France in the time of Charlemagne, the great European king of around the year 800. Jorjani says the sightings were so common that hysteria broke out at the French court, and Charlemagne considered declaring war on the "tyrants of the air", which would mean people were dealing with visitors from the sky over a thousand years ago.
